data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Matthias, meaning 'gift of God'. In the New Testament, Matthias was chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot as an apostle. The name Matheus carries the meaning “Gift of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Matheus usually hope their child will grow to embody gift of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Matheus total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.
data.cultural_impact: In many cultures, the name Matheus/Matthias is a common name and holds a significant place in history and tradition. For example, in Portugal, it is one of the most popular names for boys, as evidenced by the high number of individuals with this name in various fields including politics, arts, and sports. Additionally, in the Middle Ages, Matthias was often depicted as a saint and a patron of mental and emotional balance, representing the spiritual virtue of steadfastness.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Matheus/Matthias carries a deep spiritual significance as it means 'gift of God'. It serves as a reminder of the divine providence and the belief that every person is a unique and valuable creation of God. The choice of Matthias as an apostle in the New Testament demonstrates God's grace and favor, highlighting the importance of faith and trust in God. Additionally, the spiritual virtues associated with the name, such as steadfastness and mental and emotional balance, emphasize the importance of living a virtuous and balanced life in accordance with God's will.
